name_zh: 呼和浩特市老牛湾黄河大峡谷旅游区
address_zh: 内蒙古自治区呼和浩特市清水河县老牛湾镇老牛湾黄河大峡谷旅游区
address_en: Laoniuwan Yellow River Grand Canyon Tourist Area, Laoniuwan Town, Qingshuihe County, Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region
intro_zh: 老牛湾黄河大峡谷旅游区位于清水河县境内西南部，面积9.5平方公里，地处晋、蒙黄河大峡谷的核心地段和黄河“几”字弯腹地。老牛湾黄河大峡谷旅游区内文物古迹众多，自然人文景观皆美，历史文化底蕴深厚，30余公里的峡谷段两岸奇峰壁立、姿态万千。拥有长城与黄河唯一握手之地的独特奇观、宁边州故城遗址、全国最美古村落—老牛湾古村落、全国最大的天然石坪广场—神牛广场、具有黄河九十九道弯象征意义的九曲黄河阵、幽静深邃的杨家川小峡谷、270度大回环的太极湾、蜿蜒盘旋于峡谷的游步道。
intro_en: The Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, also known as the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon, the Tsangpo Canyon, the Brahmaputra Canyon or the Tsangpo Gorge (simplified Chinese: 雅鲁藏布大峡谷; traditional Chinese: 雅魯藏布大峽谷; pinyin: Yǎlǔzàngbù Dàxiágǔ), is a canyon along the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet Autonomous Region, China. It is the deepest canyon in the world, and at 504.6 kilometres (313.5 mi) is slightly longer than the Grand Canyon in the United States, making it one of the world's largest. The Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibetan name for the upper course of the Brahmaputra) originates near Mount Kailash and runs east for about 1,700 kilometres (1,100 mi), draining a northern section of the Himalayas before it enters the gorge just downstream of Pei, Tibet, near the settlement of Zhibe. The canyon has a length of about 240 kilometres (150 mi) as the gorge bends around Mount Namcha Barwa (7,782 metres or 25,531 feet) and cuts its way through the eastern Himalayas. Its waters drop from about 2,900 metres (9,500 ft) near Pei to about 1,500 metres (4,900 ft) at the end of the Upper Gorge where the Po Tsangpo River enters.
